tag: a compression answering "none" is recorded as raising an escalation named none
why: L1 — the defect as it stood before this round. 'escalations: none' parsed to ['none'], a non-empty list, which ESCALATES: a compression reporting nothing to escalate was recorded as escalating, and 'missing: none' fired the missing-input term the same way. It also made the no-escalation state unreachable, which is a clause of this item's bar.

tag: a blank value is read as an answer of none
why: L1's other side, and the harder direction to get right. 'escalations: ' with nothing after it is AMBIGUOUS — it may be a model that answered none or one that answered nothing at all — so the key stays ABSENT. Reading a blank as 'none' would turn a non-answer into a clearance.

tag: a comma-separated list is parsed as a single escalation
why: L1. A model asked for a list writes commas as often as semicolons, and 'escalations: a, b' parsed to ONE item reading 'a, b' — which still escalates, so nothing went visibly wrong, and the page would have shown one escalation where there were two.

tag: the record does not carry what was asked, so the page's first field has no data
why: L3. The companion surface leads with 'what was asked' and the record kept only the observation's id, surface and source — so the field the page leads with had nothing behind it and the observation that held the text was stored nowhere.

tag: an absent escalation list renders as "none raised"
why: L4, and it is the clause the whole page turns on. With the mutation a request nothing compressed renders 'None raised — the compression answered', telling a reader their request was screened and cleared when nothing read it. The three states collapse to two and the page looks entirely normal.

tag: the page drops the sentence saying an absence is not an absence of escalations
old: Its absence is not an absence of {label.toLowerCase()}.
why: L4. 'Not evaluated' alone is a label a reader can take as a formality; the sentence is what stops them reading the blank as reassurance. The probe asserts it on the rendered page and the guard asserts it in source.

tag: an unevaluated decision term renders as a pass
old: {t.fired === true ? 'FIRED' : t.fired === false ? 'did not fire' : NOT_EVALUATED}
why: L4 — 'nothing on it claims an alignment the kernel did not evaluate', the item's third clause, stated as plainly as it can be. A term the kernel could not evaluate would render exactly like one it evaluated and cleared.

tag: consumption renders a zero instead of saying nothing measured it
why: L4. P2.15 is not built, so nothing measured what any run cost. A zero that means 'not measured' is the defect this programme keeps removing, and it would be at its worst here — on the surface a user reads to understand what their request consumed.

tag: the companion surface has no route, so it is a file rather than a page
why: L4. The reach failure this plan keeps finding, in its purest form: the page exists, type-checks, and nobody can open it. The commented-out form is used deliberately because the component name still appears in the import, so a check on the NAME alone would survive it.

tag: the probe's seed hand-writes its rows instead of computing them
old: rec = kernel.build_record(obs, served_by, is_external, False, text)
why: L5. A seed that writes the records by hand makes the probe assert that the PAGE renders a dictionary — nothing about the kernel's parsing, its terms or its three states. The probe would stay green while the thing it exists to check was broken.

tag: the seed stops asserting that it produced three different states
old: assert esc[0] is None and esc[1] == [] and esc[2], (
new: assert True or esc[0] is None and esc[1] == [] and esc[2], (
why: L5. Three identical rows would make every probe check pass over a page that renders ONE state three times — the instrument agreeing with itself. The seed asserting its own premise is what makes the probe's result mean anything.
